svg.title: SM-CNN block diagram (fixed implementation)
svg.text: SM-CNN denoiser — fixed implementation (K = 24, 2,404,361 trainable parameters)
Torun et al., Signal Processing 214 (2024) 109248 · code: model/model.py · every block below has its own weights
yλ​ (squeezed to K × h × w) modulates every SSMRB → 16 SSMMs, each with its own convolutions
one skip per stage, each through its own conv 3×3 (60 → 15)
global residual learning: x̂s​ = network output + ys​
266,880 parameters per SSMRB · two SSMMs and two convolutions, none shared with other blocks
fnext​ = norm(fpre​) ⊙ (1 + γ(yλ​)) + β(yλ​) (Eq. 3, with γ re-parameterised as 1 + γ)
100,980 parameters per SSMM · γ and β come from two separate conv 3×3 heads
Fixed relative to the previous implementation
Every SSMRB, SSMM, stage conv and skip conv has its own weights (the old code reused one of each: 248,576 parameters).
γ and β are predicted by two separate conv 3×3 heads (the old code used one convolution, so γ was equal to β).
The noisy input band and the clean target are the same band, index K//2 (old: input band 11, target band 12).
Instance norm uses the biased variance of Eqs. 4–5; the constructor takes keyword arguments (old call swapped the 2D/3D filter counts).
Inference mirror-pads K//2 bands, slides a K-band window and denoises each full band, for any image size or band count.
